#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Update the local pi-mono fork from upstream, rebase local patches, rebuild the
# coding-agent so the local `pi` CLI picks up changes, and refresh extensions.
#
# Operates on ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork by default.
# Override with RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR=/path/to/fork.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
FORK_DIR="${RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR:-$HOME/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork}"
UPSTREAM_REMOTE="upstream"
ORIGIN_REMOTE="origin"
TRUNK_BRANCH="main"

if [[ ! -d "$FORK_DIR/.git" ]]; then
  echo "error: $FORK_DIR is not a git checkout" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$FORK_DIR"

# --- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------
if ! git diff --quiet || ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "error: working tree has uncommitted changes in $FORK_DIR" >&2
  echo "       commit, stash, or discard them before running update-pi" >&2
  exit 1
fi

START_BRANCH="$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "$START_BRANCH" ]]; then
  echo "error: not on a branch (detached HEAD)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

PRE_LOCK_HASH="$(shasum package-lock.json 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' || true)"

echo "→ starting branch: $START_BRANCH"

# --- fetch upstream ----------------------------------------------------------
echo "→ fetching $UPSTREAM_REMOTE"
git fetch "$UPSTREAM_REMOTE" --tags --prune

INCOMING="$(git rev-list --count "$TRUNK_BRANCH..$UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
if [[ "$INCOMING" == "0" ]]; then
  echo "→ $TRUNK_BRANCH already up to date with $UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"
else
  echo "→ $INCOMING new commits on $UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"
  git log --oneline "$TRUNK_BRANCH..$UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH" | sed 's/^/    /'
fi

# --- sync main ---------------------------------------------------------------
echo "→ syncing $TRUNK_BRANCH"
git checkout "$TRUNK_BRANCH"
if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$TRUNK_BRANCH" "$UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"; then
  git merge --ff-only "$UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"
elif git merge-base --is-ancestor "$UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH" "$TRUNK_BRANCH"; then
  echo "→ $TRUNK_BRANCH already contains $UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"
else
  echo "→ $TRUNK_BRANCH has local fork commits; merging $UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"
  git merge --no-edit "$UPSTREAM_REMOTE/$TRUNK_BRANCH"
fi
git push "$ORIGIN_REMOTE" "$TRUNK_BRANCH"

# --- rebase patch branch -----------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$START_BRANCH" != "$TRUNK_BRANCH" ]]; then
  echo "→ rebasing $START_BRANCH onto $TRUNK_BRANCH"
  git checkout "$START_BRANCH"
  if ! git rebase "$TRUNK_BRANCH"; then
    echo "" >&2
    echo "error: rebase has conflicts" >&2
    echo "       resolve in $FORK_DIR, then:" >&2
    echo "         git rebase --continue" >&2
    echo "         git push $ORIGIN_REMOTE $START_BRANCH --force-with-lease" >&2
    echo "         (cd $REPO_ROOT && scripts/update-pi)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "→ pushing $START_BRANCH (force-with-lease)"
  git push "$ORIGIN_REMOTE" "$START_BRANCH" --force-with-lease
fi

# --- install if lockfile changed ---------------------------------------------
POST_LOCK_HASH="$(shasum package-lock.json 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' || true)"
if [[ "$PRE_LOCK_HASH" != "$POST_LOCK_HASH" ]]; then
  echo "→ package-lock.json changed; running npm install"
  npm install
else
  echo "→ package-lock.json unchanged; skipping npm install"
fi

# --- build pi's dependency chain --------------------------------------------
echo "→ building tui → ai → agent → coding-agent"
( cd packages/tui          && npm run build )
( cd packages/ai           && npm run build )
( cd packages/agent        && npm run build )
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build )

# --- refresh extensions ------------------------------------------------------
# `pi update --extensions` updates packages/extensions without invoking the
# source-checkout self-updater again.
echo "→ refreshing pi extensions"
"$FORK_DIR/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js" update --extensions

# --- tokenjuice extension ----------------------------------------------------
# tokenjuice ships its Pi integration as a generated, self-contained extension
# at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js. The file is *not* refreshed by
# `pi update --extensions` (that handles Pi-package extensions only). Re-run
# `tokenjuice install pi` whenever the installed CLI version differs from the
# version stamped into the generated file.
TJ_EXT="$HOME/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js"
if command -v tokenjuice >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  TJ_CLI_VER="$(tokenjuice --version 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' v' || true)"
  TJ_EXT_VER="$(grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' "$TJ_EXT" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*tokenjuice v([0-9.]+).*/\1/' || true)"
  if [[ -z "$TJ_CLI_VER" ]]; then
    echo "→ tokenjuice CLI version unreadable; skipping extension check"
  elif [[ ! -f "$TJ_EXT" ]]; then
    echo "→ tokenjuice extension missing; running 'tokenjuice install pi'"
    tokenjuice install pi
  elif [[ "$TJ_CLI_VER" != "$TJ_EXT_VER" ]]; then
    echo "→ tokenjuice CLI v$TJ_CLI_VER ≠ extension v${TJ_EXT_VER:-unknown}; reinstalling"
    tokenjuice install pi
  else
    echo "→ tokenjuice extension up to date (v$TJ_CLI_VER)"
  fi
else
  echo "→ tokenjuice CLI not on PATH; skipping extension check"
fi

echo ""
echo "✓ pi updated. branch: $START_BRANCH"
git --no-pager log --oneline -1

---
name: pi-cache-stability
description: "Pi prompt-cache hygiene. Use when touching forkAgent, subagents, system prompt, tools, model/tool changes, plan/compaction, cacheWrite, tool search, context modes, or cache-sensitive tool APIs."
---

# Pi Cache Stability

Anthropic's prompt cache is prefix matching: cache hits require the request prefix to be **byte-identical**, use the same model, include the same tools in the same order, and still be **alive within TTL**. Pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. Keep them honest.

**Source-of-truth**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — read it before changing anything load-bearing.

**Project memory pointer**: `~/.pi/agent/memory/project/my-pi/project_cache_strategy.md`.

## When this skill applies

Load this skill any time you are about to:

- Add or modify a call to `ctx.forkAgent()` in a pi extension.
- Edit `forkAgent`, `_forkAgentFromExtension`, `runChild`, `resolveContextPolicy`, `buildSystemPrompt`, or `overrideBaseSystemPrompt` in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent`.
- Build a new background agent that runs many times per session (memory extractor, advisor probe, autoresearch worker, condensation fork).

---
name: pi-update
description: "Update the local Pi (pi-mono fork): sync from upstream, integrate fork patches, rebuild the coding-agent binary, refresh extensions. Use when updating Pi, pulling upstream into the fork, or rebuilding so the local `pi` CLI picks up code changes."
---

# Updating Pi

Pi runs from a local fork build, **not** a published package. Updating Pi means some subset of:

- **A. Sync from upstream** — pull `earendil-works/pi-mono` into the fork's `main`, push to `origin`. *Approval-sensitive (mutates remote).*
- **B. Rebuild the binary** — build the workspace so the local `pi` CLI reflects current code. *Safe, local, reversible.*
- **C. Refresh extensions** — pull Pi-package extensions + reinstall tokenjuice. *Safe, local.*

**These are independent.** Most "my code change isn't showing up" problems need only **B** (+ **C**). Do **not** run the upstream sync just to rebuild — upstream is frequently ahead and syncing is a remote-mutating, approval-sensitive operation. Pick the steps the task actually needs.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed.

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
```

**Build the dependency chain in order** (downstream packages consume upstream `dist/`):
```bash
( cd packages/tui          && npm run build )
( cd packages/ai           && npm run build )
( cd packages/agent        && npm run build )
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build )
```
Order matters: `coding-agent` imports the built output of `agent`, which imports `ai`, which imports `tui`. Build out of order and you ship stale dist.

After this, the `pi` on PATH runs the new code. For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

## See also

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — release/versioning/rollback.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.
- skill `pi-cache-stability` — before touching cache-sensitive surface.

---
name: pi-update
description: "Update the local Pi (pi-mono fork): sync from upstream, integrate fork patches, rebuild the coding-agent binary, refresh extensions. Use when updating Pi, pulling upstream into the fork, or rebuilding so the local `pi` CLI picks up code changes."
---

# Updating Pi

Pi runs from a local fork build, **not** a published package. Updating Pi means some subset of:

- **A. Sync from upstream** — pull `earendil-works/pi-mono` into the fork's `main`, push to `origin`. *Approval-sensitive (mutates remote).*
- **B. Rebuild the binary** — build the workspace so the local `pi` CLI reflects current code. *Safe, local, reversible.*
- **C. Refresh extensions** — pull Pi-package extensions + reinstall tokenjuice. *Safe, local.*

**These are independent.** Most "my code change isn't showing up" problems need only **B** (+ **C**). Do **not** run the upstream sync just to rebuild — upstream is frequently ahead and syncing is a remote-mutating, approval-sensitive operation. Pick the steps the task actually needs.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed.

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
```

**Build the dependency chain in order** (downstream packages consume upstream `dist/`):
```bash
( cd packages/tui          && npm run build )
( cd packages/ai           && npm run build )
( cd packages/agent        && npm run build )
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build )
```
Order matters: `coding-agent` imports the built output of `agent`, which imports `ai`, which imports `tui`. Build out of order and you ship stale dist.

After this, the `pi` on PATH runs the new code. For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

## See also

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — release/versioning/rollback.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.
- skill `pi-cache-stability` — before touching cache-sensitive surface.

---
name: pi-update
description: "Update the local Pi (pi-mono fork): sync from upstream, integrate fork patches, rebuild the coding-agent binary, refresh extensions. Use when updating Pi, pulling upstream into the fork, or rebuilding so the local `pi` CLI picks up code changes."
---

# Updating Pi

Pi runs from a local fork build, **not** a published package. Updating Pi means some subset of:

- **A. Sync from upstream** — pull `earendil-works/pi-mono` into the fork's `main`, push to `origin`. *Approval-sensitive (mutates remote).*
- **B. Rebuild the binary** — build the workspace so the local `pi` CLI reflects current code. *Safe, local, reversible.*
- **C. Refresh extensions** — pull Pi-package extensions + reinstall tokenjuice. *Safe, local.*

**These are independent.** Most "my code change isn't showing up" problems need only **B** (+ **C**). Do **not** run the upstream sync just to rebuild — upstream is frequently ahead and syncing is a remote-mutating, approval-sensitive operation. Pick the steps the task actually needs.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed.

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
```

**Build the dependency chain in order** (downstream packages consume upstream `dist/`):
```bash
( cd packages/tui          && npm run build )
( cd packages/ai           && npm run build )
( cd packages/agent        && npm run build )
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build )
```
Order matters: `coding-agent` imports the built output of `agent`, which imports `ai`, which imports `tui`. Build out of order and you ship stale dist.

Only these four packages are needed for the `pi` CLI — **do not** build `mom`, `web-ui`, or `pods`.

After this, the `pi` on PATH runs the new code. For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

## See also

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — release/versioning/rollback.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.
- skill `pi-cache-stability` — before touching cache-sensitive surface.

# Rusty Terminal

macOS-first terminal with a lightweight management control plane for AI coding agents.

## Quick Reference

- **Language**: Rust workspace for the desktop/kernel, SwiftUI for companion clients
- **Terminal emulation**: `libghostty-vt` behind Rusty's `rusty-terminal` boundary, with `vt100` still serving as the default bootstrap engine
- **Primary agent integration**: unmodified external CLI agents in PTYs
- **Embedded harness**: optional, provider-backed, ACP-capable but not ACP-defined
- **Remote control**: paired WebSocket JSON-RPC control plane
- **Storage**: long-term direction is SQLite index + append-only JSONL transcripts; current `v1` resume store is workspace-local under `.rusty/` with `index.json`, per-session `timeline.jsonl`, `screen-checkpoint.json`, and `session.json`
- **Async**: tokio
- **Build deps**: the repo now pins `rustc 1.94.1` via `rust-toolchain.toml`; `zig 0.16.0` is the machine default, but Ghostty upstream still builds locally through an isolated `zig@0.15.2` path today. Rusty now has a Rusty-owned dynamically loaded Ghostty backend in `crates/rusty-terminal`, selected with `RUSTY_TERMINAL_ENGINE=ghostty` and `RUSTY_GHOSTTY_VT_DYLIB=/path/to/libghostty-vt...`; the repeatable local dylib build entrypoint is `scripts/build-ghostty-vt.sh`.

Current integration decision:

- Keep Rust current at stable.
- Do not treat the tested `~/Projects/oss/libghostty-rs` wrapper as Rusty's architectural default.
- Isolate Ghostty-specific Zig constraints to the Ghostty integration path rather than making them the global project rule.
- Prefer a Rusty-owned narrow Ghostty FFI layer if the reference wrapper continues to lag current Zig.

## Architecture

See `PLAN.md` for the current architecture and phase ordering.

Current top-level modules:

- `rusty-core` — session model, control plane, approvals, notifications
- `rusty-store` — SQLite indexes, JSONL transcripts, replay
- `rusty-terminal` — PTY lifecycle, VT wrapper, OSC/DCS, shell hooks
- `rusty-providers` — Claude/Codex/Pi detection and provider adapters
- `rusty-harness` — embedded harness manager and backends
- `rusty-ssh` — SSH detection, bootstrap, tmux control mode, remote proxying
- `rusty-remote` — pairing, auth, WebSocket JSON-RPC API
- `rusty-ui` / `rusty-app` — local desktop shell and renderer boundary

## External Source References

3rd-party reference checkouts live under `~/Projects/oss/` per workspace convention (not part of this repo, full git history). Notable entries used by Rusty:

- `~/Projects/oss/ghostty/` — ghostty source / `libghostty-vt` headers (build target for `scripts/build-ghostty-vt.sh`)
- `~/Projects/oss/ghostling/` — minimal C terminal reference
- `~/Projects/oss/libghostty-rs/` — Rust FFI wrapper (not Rusty's architectural default; see above)
- `~/Projects/oss/codex/` — Codex CLI + app-server
- `~/Projects/oss/openai-agents-python/`, `openai-agents-js/` — Agents SDKs
- `~/Projects/oss/pi-mono/` — pi monorepo (upstream); review `packages/coding-agent` APIs for ToolSearch/deferred tools, extension runtime loading, agent task tracking, and TUI runner/dashboard ideas
- `~/Projects/oss/opencode/`, `fluid-functionalism/`, `zed/`, `awesome-libghostty/`
- `~/Projects/oss/warp-terminal/` — Warp terminal upstream (read-only reference)

Local forks (separate repos, outside `oss/`):

- `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/` — Luke's pi fork (`valkyriweb/pi-mono`, upstream `badlogic/pi-mono`); managed by `scripts/update-pi`

## Conventions

- Keep the product PTY-first. External CLI agents are the default path.
- Treat ACP as a harness backend, not the global architecture.
- Keep rendering behind a replaceable boundary.
- Prefer the simplest solution that honestly satisfies the current phase before reaching for more machinery, abstraction, or protocol surface.
- Use the `oracle` skill on difficult, high-uncertainty, or architecture-shaping tasks for design checks and cross-validation, but treat Oracle as a tool for pressure-testing a simple approach, not for justifying unnecessary complexity.
- Favor thin vertical slices with verification before expanding scope.
- Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` before committing once code exists.

## Research Notes

Design notes and source-backed research live in `research/`. Read before touching the relevant subsystem:

- `research/prompt-cache-preservation.md` — prompt-cache rules for `rusty-providers` (prefix-stable serialisation, accumulate-then-parse, soft-fail tool args, non-streaming retry, cache-breakpoint API). Cache hit rate is the per-tenant margin.
- `research/warp-client-reference.md` — Warp open-source client lessons, the possible Warp-fork-as-client path, and provider switching across Pi, Claude Code CLI, and Codex CLI.
- `research/pi-agent-api-reference.md` — Pi coding-agent API patterns worth studying for Rusty's main TUI session runner, active-session tracking, ToolSearch/deferred actions, extension runtime lifecycle, and task/status dashboard.

# `update-pi-agent` — pi source-checkout update wrapper

**Path:** `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent`

> The manual `scripts/update-pi` script was retired. The canonical "how to update pi"
> process (upstream sync, fork patches, build chain, extensions, gates) now lives in the
> **`pi-update` skill**: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/pi-update/SKILL.md`.
> When updating Pi by hand, follow that skill. This doc covers only the automated
> `pi update` wrapper.

## Why a wrapper exists

Built-in `pi update` refreshes extensions but **cannot** self-update a source-checkout
install — it errors:

> error: pi cannot self-update this installation.
> Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper,
> or source checkout that provides this installation.

So `pi update` routes source-checkout self-updates through this wrapper via global settings:

```json
"sourceUpdateCommand": ["/Users/luke/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent"]
```

## What the wrapper does

`update-pi-agent` launches a bounded, non-interactive Pi maintenance session
(`pi --print --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write`) that:

- prepares an **update branch/worktree** (never mutates the daily `main` checkout),
- merges `upstream/main` into it,
- runs a health check (`npm run check`),
- reports the PR command.

It deliberately does **not** merge into daily `main`, push, or resolve conflicts automatically.

### Wrapper defaults

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH` | `lue/pi-upstream-<timestamp>` |
| `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE` | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update` |
| `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK` | `npm run check` |
| `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN` | pi binary override (if the shell `pi` shim is wrong) |

## Conflict recovery

If the update-branch merge conflicts, fix inside the update worktree, then:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update
git merge --continue
npm run check
git push -u origin <update-branch>
```

Consult `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` for the fork's divergence
ledger before resolving non-trivial conflicts. Don't `git stash` for pi maintenance — it mixes
work streams and complicates recovery.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed.

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
```

**Build the dependency chain in order** (downstream packages consume upstream `dist/`):
```bash
( cd packages/tui          && npm run build )
( cd packages/ai           && npm run build )
( cd packages/agent        && npm run build )
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build )
```
Order matters: `coding-agent` imports the built output of `agent`, which imports `ai`, which imports `tui`. Build out of order and you ship stale dist.

Only these four packages are needed for the `pi` CLI — **do not** build `mom`, `web-ui`, or `pods`.

After this, the `pi` on PATH runs the new code. For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

### Codex adapter prompt patch  *(re-verify after every extension refresh)*

`pi update --extensions` can overwrite Luke's local prompt patch in the Codex conversion adapter. After refreshing, confirm the patch survived in `CODEX_GUIDELINES`:
```bash
PATCH="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.14.0/installation/lib/node_modules/@howaboua/pi-codex-conversion/src/prompt/build-system-prompt.ts"
grep -nE 'timeout_seconds|tokenjuice wrap|raw logs|write_stdin' "$PATCH"
```
The patch teaches the Codex adapter to: set `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_ms` on hang-prone commands; use `tokenjuice wrap`/`reduce` for noisy output; reduce at source with `jq`/`rg`/`head`/`tail`/`sed -n`; not dump raw logs/JSONL/k8s/traces unless asked; stop polling `write_stdin` after two empty reads. Re-apply if missing. (The `v24.14.0` path drifts with the active fnm Node version — adjust if needed.)

## How `pi update` triggers this  *(source-checkout self-update)*

Built-in `pi update` refreshes extensions but **cannot** self-update a source-checkout install — it errors:
> error: pi cannot self-update this installation. Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.

So source-checkout updates are routed through a bounded Pi maintenance session via global settings:
```json
"sourceUpdateCommand": ["/Users/luke/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent"]
```
`scripts/update-pi-agent` launches a non-interactive `pi --print --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write` session that prepares an **update branch/worktree**, merges `upstream/main` there, health-checks (`npm run check`), and reports the PR command — deliberately **not** mutating the daily `main` checkout. Wrapper env defaults: `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH` (`lue/pi-upstream-<ts>`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE` (`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK` (`npm run check`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN` (pi binary override). When you (an agent) run the update by hand instead, follow sections A–C above directly.

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

## See also

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — release/versioning/rollback.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.
- skill `pi-cache-stability` — before touching cache-sensitive surface.

---
name: pi-update
description: "Update the local Pi (pi-mono fork): sync from upstream, integrate fork patches, rebuild the coding-agent binary, refresh extensions. Use when updating Pi, pulling upstream into the fork, or rebuilding so the local `pi` CLI picks up code changes."
---

# Updating Pi

Pi runs from a local fork build, **not** a published package. Updating Pi means some subset of:

- **A. Sync from upstream** — pull `earendil-works/pi-mono` into the fork's `main`, push to `origin`. *Approval-sensitive (mutates remote).*
- **B. Rebuild the binary** — build the workspace so the local `pi` CLI reflects current code. *Safe, local, reversible.*
- **C. Refresh extensions** — pull Pi-package extensions + reinstall tokenjuice. *Safe, local.*

**These are independent.** Pick the steps the task needs:

- **Full update** ("update pi" / "pull upstream") → do **A → B → C** in order: sync from upstream, rebuild, refresh extensions.
- **My code change isn't live** → just **B** (+ **C** if extensions changed). Do **not** sync upstream merely to rebuild — that's a separate, remote-mutating, approval-sensitive decision.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed. (`pi update` from a source checkout routes through the `update-pi-agent` wrapper — see the bottom section.)

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
```

**Build the dependency chain in order** (downstream packages consume upstream `dist/`):
```bash
( cd packages/tui          && npm run build )
( cd packages/ai           && npm run build )
( cd packages/agent        && npm run build )
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build )
```
Order matters: `coding-agent` imports the built output of `agent`, which imports `ai`, which imports `tui`. Build out of order and you ship stale dist.

Only these four packages are needed for the `pi` CLI — **do not** build `mom`, `web-ui`, or `pods`.

After this, the `pi` on PATH runs the new code. For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

### Codex adapter prompt patch  *(re-verify after every extension refresh)*

`pi update --extensions` can overwrite Luke's local prompt patch in the Codex conversion adapter. After refreshing, confirm the patch survived in `CODEX_GUIDELINES`:
```bash
PATCH="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.14.0/installation/lib/node_modules/@howaboua/pi-codex-conversion/src/prompt/build-system-prompt.ts"
grep -nE 'timeout_seconds|tokenjuice wrap|raw logs|write_stdin' "$PATCH"
```
The patch teaches the Codex adapter to: set `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_ms` on hang-prone commands; use `tokenjuice wrap`/`reduce` for noisy output; reduce at source with `jq`/`rg`/`head`/`tail`/`sed -n`; not dump raw logs/JSONL/k8s/traces unless asked; stop polling `write_stdin` after two empty reads. Re-apply if missing. (The `v24.14.0` path drifts with the active fnm Node version — adjust if needed.)

## How `pi update` triggers this  *(source-checkout self-update)*

Built-in `pi update` refreshes extensions but **cannot** self-update a source-checkout install — it errors:
> error: pi cannot self-update this installation. Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.

So source-checkout updates are routed through a bounded Pi maintenance session via global settings:
```json
"sourceUpdateCommand": ["/Users/luke/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent"]
```
`scripts/update-pi-agent` launches a non-interactive `pi --print --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write` session that prepares an **update branch/worktree**, merges `upstream/main` there, health-checks (`npm run check`), and reports the PR command — deliberately **not** mutating the daily `main` checkout. Wrapper env defaults: `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH` (`lue/pi-upstream-<ts>`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE` (`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK` (`npm run check`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN` (pi binary override). When you (an agent) run the update by hand instead, follow sections A–C above directly.

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

## See also

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — release/versioning/rollback.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.
- skill `pi-cache-stability` — before touching cache-sensitive surface.

The cd-waste task had two halves: **(a)** the core `workdir` param — already drafted as `DRAFT-cd-waste-fix.md` (GO-6, gated on Luke since it's a critical-tier core fork patch), and **(b)** an *interim* absolute-paths/never-cd directive — the extension-side, cache-safe, autonomous-implementable companion. 1	# DRAFT (for review) — cd-waste fix: a first-class `workdir` param on bash
2	
3	**Status:** DRAFT — NOT applied. Critical-tier (core tool, every session, every command) → show diff, get Luke's go, then apply to a pi-mono-fork branch + build-gate.
4	**Why:** Measured #1 gap. Pi ~24 `cd`-bearing bash calls/session (48% of bash) vs Codex ~0.25 (0.08%). Codex's `exec_command` takes a `workdir` param (set on 99% of calls) → the model never needs `cd`. See `MEASURED-GAPS.md`.
5	
6	## Root cause (verified in source)
7	
8	Pi's bash tool already blocks **redundant** cd (`bash.ts:1058` `redundantCdToCurrentWorkingDirectory` → `redundantCdError`, points to `git -C`/`npm --prefix`), and `native-tool-overrides` strips a leading `cd <cwd> &&` (`index.ts:261` `stripRedundantCd`). But the tool has **no per-call working directory** — `createBashToolDefinition(cwd, …)` bakes the session `cwd` as a closure, and `execute()` destructures only `{command, timeout, run_in_background, tui_only}`. So to operate in *another* dir the model must `cd /other && …` (or use per-command flags). That non-redundant `cd` is the measured waste. The existing `prepareArguments` extension hook only sees args, not the spawn cwd, so this **cannot** be fixed extension-only — it needs a small generic core primitive (pi-dev.md: justified core patch).
9	
10	## Proposed core patch — `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`
11	
12	### 1. Add `workdir` to `bashSchema` (after `command`, ~line 29)
13	```ts
14		command: Type.String({ description: "Bash command to execute" }),
15	+	workdir: Type.Optional(
16	+		Type.String({
17	+			description:
18	+				"Absolute path (or path relative to the session cwd) to run the command in. Use this INSTEAD of `cd <dir> && …` when you need a different directory — e.g. workdir:\"/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi\". Defaults to the session working directory.",
19	+		}),
20	+	),
21		timeout: Type.Optional(/* … unchanged … */),
22	```
23	
24	### 2. Read it in `execute()` (destructure, ~line 1216) and resolve an effective cwd
25	```ts
26		async execute(
27			_toolCallId,
28	-		{ command, timeout, run_in_background, tui_only }: { command: string; timeout?: number | false; run_in_background?: boolean; tui_only?: boolean },
29	+		{ command, workdir, timeout, run_in_background, tui_only }: { command: string; workdir?: string; timeout?: number | false; run_in_background?: boolean; tui_only?: boolean },
30			signal?, onUpdate?, _ctx?,
31		) {
32	+		// Per-call working directory (Codex exec_command parity). Absolute paths win;
33	+		// relative paths resolve against the session cwd. Existence is validated
34	+		// downstream (createLocalBashOperations / spawnBashBackground both throw on a
35	+		// missing dir), so a bad workdir surfaces as a clear "Working directory does
36	+		// not exist" error instead of silently running in the wrong place.
37	+		const effectiveCwd = workdir ? resolve(cwd, workdir) : cwd;
38	```
39	Then replace the three `cwd` uses inside `execute()` with `effectiveCwd`:
40	- `redundantCdToCurrentWorkingDirectory(command, cwd)` → `…(command, effectiveCwd)` (line ~1237)
41	- `spawnBashBackground(command, cwd, …)` → `spawnBashBackground(command, effectiveCwd, …)` (line ~1260)
42	- `resolveSpawnContext(resolvedCommand, cwd, spawnHook)` → `…(resolvedCommand, effectiveCwd, spawnHook)` (line ~1283)
43	
44	(`resolve` is already imported from `node:path`, line 5. No other call sites touch `cwd`.)
45	
46	### 3. Description nudge (so the model reaches for `workdir`, not `cd`)
47	`bash.ts:1200` description, change the opening + add a guideline at `promptGuidelines` (~line 1204):
48	```ts
49	-		description: `Execute a bash command in the current working directory. …`,
50	+		description: `Execute a bash command. Runs in the session working directory by default; pass \`workdir\` (absolute path) to run elsewhere instead of \`cd <dir> && …\`. …`,
51			promptGuidelines: [
52	+			"To run in a different directory, pass `workdir` (absolute path) — never `cd <dir> && …`. The session cwd is the default.",
53				/* …existing… */
54			],
55	```
56	
57	## Companion extension nudge (extension-first, can land independently, lower risk)
58	`my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts:250` — the Bash description override already rewrites text; append a `workdir` pointer there too so Luke's `Bash` alias advertises it. Gated by `test:extension-gate` + `native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.
59	
60	## pi-fork-patch-inventory.md entry (required by pi-dev.md)
61	> **bash `workdir` param** — added optional per-call working directory to the core bash tool (`tools/bash.ts`). Generic platform primitive; can't be exposed via the `prepareArguments` hook (no access to spawn cwd). Codex `exec_command` parity. Eliminates the measured ~24 `cd`/session waste. Refresh: re-run `tools/measure-pi-sessions.mjs` after a few sessions; cd-rate should fall toward CC/Codex.
62	
63	## Gate + verify plan
64	1. `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate` (184 e2e + my-pi extension gate).
65	2. `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.
66	3. Add a unit test: `workdir:"/tmp"` runs there; bad `workdir` → "Working directory does not exist"; redundant-cd guard still fires against `effectiveCwd`.
67	4. Dogfood on the built artifact, then re-run `measure-pi-sessions.mjs` over the next ~10 sessions → expect cd-rate ↓.
68	
69	## Risk / rollback
70	- **Cache:** adds one optional property to `bashSchema` → the bash tool's `tools[]` bytes change once → a single cold re-warm for all sessions, then stable. Acceptable, expected. No per-session variability introduced.
71	- **Behaviour:** purely additive; omitting `workdir` is byte-identical behaviour to today. The redundant-cd guard now keys off `effectiveCwd` (correct — a `cd <workdir> && …` inside an explicit workdir is still redundant).
72	- **Rollback:** revert the bash.ts hunk; schema returns to 4 fields. Reversible.
73	
74	## Interim (zero-code) option if Luke wants to defer the core patch
75	Strengthen only the directive/description (extension layer): "never `cd`; use `git -C`/`npm --prefix`/absolute paths." Cheaper, but won't fully close the gap — some multi-command sequences in another dir genuinely want `workdir`. The param is the real fix.

# DRAFT (for review) — cd-waste fix: a first-class `workdir` param on bash

**Status:** DRAFT — NOT applied. Critical-tier (core tool, every session, every command) → show diff, get Luke's go, then apply to a pi-mono-fork branch + build-gate.
**Why:** Measured #1 gap. Pi ~24 `cd`-bearing bash calls/session (48% of bash) vs Codex ~0.25 (0.08%). Codex's `exec_command` takes a `workdir` param (set on 99% of calls) → the model never needs `cd`. See `MEASURED-GAPS.md`.

## Root cause (verified in source)

Pi's bash tool already blocks **redundant** cd (`bash.ts:1058` `redundantCdToCurrentWorkingDirectory` → `redundantCdError`, points to `git -C`/`npm --prefix`), and `native-tool-overrides` strips a leading `cd <cwd> &&` (`index.ts:261` `stripRedundantCd`). But the tool has **no per-call working directory** — `createBashToolDefinition(cwd, …)` bakes the session `cwd` as a closure, and `execute()` destructures only `{command, timeout, run_in_background, tui_only}`. So to operate in *another* dir the model must `cd /other && …` (or use per-command flags). That non-redundant `cd` is the measured waste. The existing `prepareArguments` extension hook only sees args, not the spawn cwd, so this **cannot** be fixed extension-only — it needs a small generic core primitive (pi-dev.md: justified core patch).

## Proposed core patch — `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`

### 1. Add `workdir` to `bashSchema` (after `command`, ~line 29)
```ts
	command: Type.String({ description: "Bash command to execute" }),
+	workdir: Type.Optional(
+		Type.String({
+			description:
+				"Absolute path (or path relative to the session cwd) to run the command in. Use this INSTEAD of `cd <dir> && …` when you need a different directory — e.g. workdir:\"/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi\". Defaults to the session working directory.",
+		}),
+	),
	timeout: Type.Optional(/* … unchanged … */),
```

### 2. Read it in `execute()` (destructure, ~line 1216) and resolve an effective cwd
```ts
	async execute(
		_toolCallId,
-		{ command, timeout, run_in_background, tui_only }: { command: string; timeout?: number | false; run_in_background?: boolean; tui_only?: boolean },
+		{ command, workdir, timeout, run_in_background, tui_only }: { command: string; workdir?: string; timeout?: number | false; run_in_background?: boolean; tui_only?: boolean },
		signal?, onUpdate?, _ctx?,
	) {
+		// Per-call working directory (Codex exec_command parity). Absolute paths win;
+		// relative paths resolve against the session cwd. Existence is validated
+		// downstream (createLocalBashOperations / spawnBashBackground both throw on a
+		// missing dir), so a bad workdir surfaces as a clear "Working directory does
+		// not exist" error instead of silently running in the wrong place.
+		const effectiveCwd = workdir ? resolve(cwd, workdir) : cwd;
```
Then replace the three `cwd` uses inside `execute()` with `effectiveCwd`:
- `redundantCdToCurrentWorkingDirectory(command, cwd)` → `…(command, effectiveCwd)` (line ~1237)
- `spawnBashBackground(command, cwd, …)` → `spawnBashBackground(command, effectiveCwd, …)` (line ~1260)
- `resolveSpawnContext(resolvedCommand, cwd, spawnHook)` → `…(resolvedCommand, effectiveCwd, spawnHook)` (line ~1283)

(`resolve` is already imported from `node:path`, line 5. No other call sites touch `cwd`.)

### 3. Description nudge (so the model reaches for `workdir`, not `cd`)
`bash.ts:1200` description, change the opening + add a guideline at `promptGuidelines` (~line 1204):
```ts
-		description: `Execute a bash command in the current working directory. …`,
+		description: `Execute a bash command. Runs in the session working directory by default; pass \`workdir\` (absolute path) to run elsewhere instead of \`cd <dir> && …\`. …`,
		promptGuidelines: [
+			"To run in a different directory, pass `workdir` (absolute path) — never `cd <dir> && …`. The session cwd is the default.",
			/* …existing… */
		],
```

## Companion extension nudge (extension-first, can land independently, lower risk)
`my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts:250` — the Bash description override already rewrites text; append a `workdir` pointer there too so Luke's `Bash` alias advertises it. Gated by `test:extension-gate` + `native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## pi-fork-patch-inventory.md entry (required by pi-dev.md)
> **bash `workdir` param** — added optional per-call working directory to the core bash tool (`tools/bash.ts`). Generic platform primitive; can't be exposed via the `prepareArguments` hook (no access to spawn cwd). Codex `exec_command` parity. Eliminates the measured ~24 `cd`/session waste. Refresh: re-run `tools/measure-pi-sessions.mjs` after a few sessions; cd-rate should fall toward CC/Codex.

## Gate + verify plan
1. `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate` (184 e2e + my-pi extension gate).
2. `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.
3. Add a unit test: `workdir:"/tmp"` runs there; bad `workdir` → "Working directory does not exist"; redundant-cd guard still fires against `effectiveCwd`.
4. Dogfood on the built artifact, then re-run `measure-pi-sessions.mjs` over the next ~10 sessions → expect cd-rate ↓.

## Risk / rollback
- **Cache:** adds one optional property to `bashSchema` → the bash tool's `tools[]` bytes change once → a single cold re-warm for all sessions, then stable. Acceptable, expected. No per-session variability introduced.
- **Behaviour:** purely additive; omitting `workdir` is byte-identical behaviour to today. The redundant-cd guard now keys off `effectiveCwd` (correct — a `cd <workdir> && …` inside an explicit workdir is still redundant).

export const meta = {
  name: 'cd-waste-interim-directive',
  description: 'Design + adversarially verify the interim never-cd directive for Pi bash (extension layer), as a gate-able worktree draft',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Investigate', detail: 'best extension-layer injection site + per-turn token cost' },
    { title: 'Design', detail: '3 independent directive drafts + judge panel' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial cache-stability + correctness review of the winner' },
  ],
}

// ---------- shared context handed to every agent (they have ZERO prior context) ----------
const CTX = `
CONTEXT — Pi coding-agent harness (fork of pi-mono). Measured #1 inefficiency vs Claude Code / Codex:
Pi emits ~24 \`cd\`-bearing bash calls/session (48% of bash calls) vs Codex ~0.25 (0.08%). Codex avoids
\`cd\` because its exec_command takes a first-class \`workdir\` param. Pi's bash tool has NO per-call
workdir yet (a core fork patch for that is separately drafted and GATED on Luke — DO NOT rely on it).

THIS TASK = the INTERIM directive that can land NOW, before the core workdir param:
strengthen the model-facing guidance so the model stops using \`cd <dir> && …\` and instead uses
techniques that ALREADY work today: ABSOLUTE PATHS, \`git -C <dir>\`, \`npm --prefix <dir>\`, tool flags.

HARD CONSTRAINTS (a draft that violates any of these is invalid):
1. MUST NOT reference a \`workdir\` parameter — it does not exist yet; advertising it would tell the
   model to pass a param the bash schema rejects.
2. Lives in the EXTENSION layer, gated by \`test:extension-gate\` (NOT the core fork — that's the gated patch).
3. The natural injection point is the Bash tool DESCRIPTION override in
   \`~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts\` (lines ~248-271), which already
   appends a literal sentence to core's bash description. EXACT current appended text:
     " Foreground \`sleep\` is blocked (alone or chained with && / ;) — use monitor_start with an
       until-loop to wait on a condition, or run_in_background: true to wait for a command you started."
4. The \`bash\` tool is \`alwaysLoad: true\` → its description is in tools[] and BILLED EVERY TURN of EVERY
   session, forever. So brevity is critical: every word has a permanent per-turn token cost. Aim ≤ ~30 words.
5. Pi ALREADY blocks REDUNDANT cd (\`cd <cwd> && …\` to the current dir) two ways: core
   \`redundantCdToCurrentWorkingDirectory\` (bash.ts) and the extension's \`stripRedundantCd\` (index.ts:261).
   The directive must target NON-redundant cd (cd to ANOTHER dir), and must NOT contradict those guards.
6. Must be byte-STATIC: no per-session, per-cwd, or time-varying interpolation (cache prefix stability).

Repos: extension lab \`~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts\`;
core bash tool \`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts\`.
Read targeted regions only (bash.ts is ~1300+ lines).
`

// ============================ Phase 1 — Investigate ============================
phase('Investigate')

const INJECTION_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['options', 'recommendation'],
  properties: {
    options: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['site', 'filePathLine', 'whereInRequest', 'billing', 'cacheStability', 'pros', 'cons'],
        properties: {
          site: { type: 'string', description: 'e.g. bash description append / bash promptGuidelines / profile-base system directive' },
          filePathLine: { type: 'string' },
          whereInRequest: { type: 'string', description: 'where this text lands in the provider request (tools[] vs system prompt vs message)' },
          billing: { type: 'string', enum: ['billed-every-turn', 'system-prompt-once-per-prefix', 'other'] },
          cacheStability: { type: 'string', description: 'byte-stable across same-cwd sessions? any variability?' },
          pros: { type: 'string' },
          cons: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    recommendation: {
      type: 'object',
      additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['site', 'filePathLine', 'why'],
      properties: { site: { type: 'string' }, filePathLine: { type: 'string' }, why: { type: 'string' } },
    },
  },
}

const TOKENCOST_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['bashIsAlwaysLoad', 'descriptionBilledEveryTurn', 'descriptionIsPerCwd', 'currentAppendedSentencePresent', 'promptGuidelinesRendered', 'notes'],
  properties: {
    bashIsAlwaysLoad: { type: 'boolean' },
    descriptionBilledEveryTurn: { type: 'boolean', description: 'is the bash description in tools[] on every turn?' },
    descriptionIsPerCwd: { type: 'boolean', description: 'does core bake the literal cwd path into the description string?' },
    currentAppendedSentencePresent: { type: 'boolean', description: 'is the foreground-sleep sentence actually present in the built description?' },
    promptGuidelinesRendered: { type: 'string', description: 'does bash promptGuidelines render to the model, and where/how often? cite file:line' },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

const [injection, tokencost] = await parallel([
  () => agent(
    `${CTX}\n\nINVESTIGATE: enumerate every EXTENSION-LAYER site where a never-cd directive could reach the model, ` +
    `and rank them by per-turn token cost + cache-stability. Candidate sites: (a) the Bash tool DESCRIPTION append in ` +
    `native-tool-overrides/index.ts; (b) the bash tool's \`promptGuidelines\` field (check bash.ts for how promptGuidelines ` +
    `is defined and whether/where Pi renders it to the model — system prompt once? per tool? grep the coding-agent src for where ` +
    `promptGuidelines is consumed); (c) any profile-level system-prompt directive seam in my-pi (e.g. pi-memory/profile-base.ts — ` +
    `NOTE this is flagged cache-critical, treat as last resort). For each: exact file:line, where the text lands in the provider ` +
    `request, whether it is billed every turn or once per cached prefix, and cache-stability. Recommend ONE site. ` +
    `Use Read/Glob; the codedb hook blocks grep/rg in Bash — use Read or the Explore agent is unavailable, so Read targeted regions.`,
    { label: 'investigate:injection-site', phase: 'Investigate', schema: INJECTION_SCHEMA },
  ),
  () => agent(
    `${CTX}\n\nMEASURE the token-cost + cache facts of the Bash DESCRIPTION-append site. Read ` +
    `native-tool-overrides/index.ts lines 240-292 and core bash.ts around the description (search the file for the string ` +
    `"Execute a bash command"). Determine: is bash alwaysLoad? Is its description in tools[] every turn (billed every turn)? ` +
    `Does core's bash description interpolate the literal cwd path (making it per-cwd)? Is the existing foreground-sleep ` +
    `appended sentence actually in the built description string? Does bash \`promptGuidelines\` get rendered to the model ` +
    `(cite where it is consumed)? Be precise and cite file:line.`,
    { label: 'investigate:token-cost', phase: 'Investigate', schema: TOKENCOST_SCHEMA },
  ),
])

log(`Injection rec: ${injection?.recommendation?.site ?? 'n/a'} @ ${injection?.recommendation?.filePathLine ?? '?'}`)
log(`alwaysLoad=${tokencost?.bashIsAlwaysLoad} billedEveryTurn=${tokencost?.descriptionBilledEveryTurn} perCwd=${tokencost?.descriptionIsPerCwd}`)

// ============================ Phase 2 — Design ============================
phase('Design')

const factPack = `
PHASE-1 FACTS (use these — they are ground-truthed):
- Recommended injection site: ${JSON.stringify(injection?.recommendation ?? 'description-append (fallback)')}
- All injection options: ${JSON.stringify(injection?.options ?? [])}
- Token/cache facts: ${JSON.stringify(tokencost ?? {})}
`

const DRAFT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['framing', 'directiveText', 'wordCount', 'injectionSite', 'referencesWorkdir', 'techniquesMentioned', 'rationale'],
  properties: {
    framing: { type: 'string' },
    directiveText: { type: 'string', description: 'the EXACT literal text to append/inject — what the model will read' },
    wordCount: { type: 'integer' },
    injectionSite: { type: 'string', description: 'where it goes (file:line / field)' },
    referencesWorkdir: { type: 'boolean', description: 'MUST be false' },
    techniquesMentioned: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    rationale: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

const FRAMINGS = [
  { key: 'terse-rule', instruction: 'Terse imperative rule. Maximum signal, minimum words. One sentence, ≤ ~22 words.' },
  { key: 'technique-list', instruction: 'A compact "do this instead" listing the concrete alternatives (git -C, npm --prefix, absolute paths, tool flags). ≤ ~30 words.' },
  { key: 'contrast', instruction: 'Brief wrong→right contrast that shows cd<dir>&&… is wasteful and names the alternative inline. ≤ ~30 words.' },
]

const drafts = (await parallel(FRAMINGS.map((f) => () =>
  agent(
    `${CTX}\n${factPack}\n\nWRITE the interim never-cd directive in this framing: ${f.instruction}\n` +
    `Return the EXACT literal text the model will read. Honor ALL hard constraints (no workdir reference; ` +
    `target non-redundant cd; don't contradict the redundant-cd guards; byte-static; terse for alwaysLoad). ` +
    `It will be appended to the Bash description right after the foreground-sleep sentence (or the phase-1 recommended site).`,
    { label: `design:${f.key}`, phase: 'Design', schema: DRAFT_SCHEMA },
  ),
))).filter(Boolean)

const JUDGE_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['scores', 'winnerText', 'winnerInjectionSite', 'synthesisNotes'],
  properties: {
    scores: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['framing', 'efficacy', 'brevity', 'cacheSafety', 'voiceFit', 'total', 'note'],
        properties: {
          framing: { type: 'string' },
          efficacy: { type: 'integer', description: '1-5: will it actually make the model stop cd-ing' },
          brevity: { type: 'integer', description: '1-5: token-cost (5 = shortest); critical because billed every turn' },
          cacheSafety: { type: 'integer', description: '1-5' },
          voiceFit: { type: 'integer', description: '1-5: matches existing terse description voice' },
          total: { type: 'integer' },
          note: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    winnerText: { type: 'string', description: 'the final synthesized directive text (may graft best bits across drafts)' },
    winnerInjectionSite: { type: 'string' },
    synthesisNotes: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

const judged = await agent(
  `${CTX}\n${factPack}\n\nYou are the JUDGE. Here are ${drafts.length} candidate directive drafts:\n` +
  `${JSON.stringify(drafts, null, 2)}\n\n` +
  `Score each on efficacy / brevity / cacheSafety / voiceFit (1-5 each). Brevity is weighted heavily — this text is ` +
  `billed every turn of every session forever. Then produce the WINNER: pick the best, grafting the strongest phrasing ` +
  `from the others. The winner MUST honor every hard constraint. Keep it to one tight sentence if possible.`,
  { label: 'design:judge', phase: 'Design', schema: JUDGE_SCHEMA },
)

log(`Winner (${judged?.winnerText?.split(/\s+/).length ?? '?'} words): ${judged?.winnerText ?? 'n/a'}`)

// ============================ Phase 3 — Verify ============================
phase('Verify')

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['approved', 'referencesUnshippedWorkdir', 'introducesPerSessionVariability', 'contradictsRedundantCdGuard', 'tooVerboseForAlwaysLoad', 'overClaims', 'issues', 'suggestedFix'],
  properties: {
    approved: { type: 'boolean' },
    referencesUnshippedWorkdir: { type: 'boolean' },
    introducesPerSessionVariability: { type: 'boolean' },
    contradictsRedundantCdGuard: { type: 'boolean' },
    tooVerboseForAlwaysLoad: { type: 'boolean' },
    overClaims: { type: 'boolean', description: 'does it claim something false, e.g. that cd never works?' },
    issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    suggestedFix: { type: 'string', description: 'if not approved, the corrected text' },
  },
}

const LENSES = [
  { key: 'cache', lens: 'CACHE-STABILITY: verify the text is byte-static (no per-session/per-cwd/time interpolation), and that adding it is only a one-time tools[] re-warm, not recurring variability. Re-read native-tool-overrides/index.ts to confirm the append is a static literal.' },
  { key: 'correctness', lens: 'CORRECTNESS: verify it does NOT reference a workdir param; does NOT contradict the redundant-cd guards (it targets cd to ANOTHER dir); names only techniques that work today (git -C / npm --prefix / absolute paths / flags); does not over-claim (cd is not forbidden outright, just discouraged as waste). Re-read bash.ts redundant-cd logic + index.ts stripRedundantCd.' },
]

const verdicts = (await parallel(LENSES.map((l) => () =>
  agent(
    `${CTX}\n\nYou are an adversarial reviewer. Try to REFUTE this proposed interim directive. Default to approved=false if uncertain.\n` +
    `PROPOSED TEXT: ${JSON.stringify(judged?.winnerText ?? '')}\n` +
    `PROPOSED SITE: ${JSON.stringify(judged?.winnerInjectionSite ?? '')}\n\n` +
    `Your lens — ${l.lens}\n\nReturn a verdict; if you reject, give the corrected text in suggestedFix.`,
    { label: `verify:${l.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA },
  ),
))).filter(Boolean)

const approved = verdicts.every((v) => v.approved)

return {
  injectionRecommendation: injection?.recommendation,
  tokenCostFacts: tokencost,
  draftCount: drafts.length,
  judgeScores: judged?.scores,
  winnerText: judged?.winnerText,
  winnerInjectionSite: judged?.winnerInjectionSite,
  synthesisNotes: judged?.synthesisNotes,
  verdicts,
  approved,
}
